{"kind":"reasoning","id":"p64-10fcfbb1","text":"The user wants to broaden to symbols that signal cleaning/clean, not strictly a broom. Good — there are monochrome Unicode symbols for cleaning:
- U+2728 ✨ sparkles (clean/shine) — emoji-ish but text presentation available (✨ U+2728 has text presentation). Canvas may render it as color emoji by default! Actually U+2728 is Emoji_Presentation=No (text presentation by default), so it should render monochrome with the font stack. Let me verify.
- U+2726 ✦ black four-pointed star (clean/shine)
- U+2B50 ⭐ star (emoji presentation).
- U+25A1 □ (clean square) no.
- U+2318 ⌘ no.
- U+2744 ❄ snowflake (clean/fresh) — emoji presentation? U+2744 has text presentation by default (❄︎), often rendered as text snowflake in symbol fonts.
- U+2696 ⚖ no.
- U+2672 ♲ recycling (clean/recycle) — text.
- U+267B ♻ recycling (emoji).
- U+1F9FD 🧽 sponge — emoji only.
- U+1F9FB 🧻 roll of paper — emoji.
- U+1F6BF 🚿 shower — emoji.
- U+2668 ☨? 
- "Broom" alternatives: U+2E19 ⸙ palm branch; U+2698 ⚘ flower.
- `⌫` erase/backspace signals "clean up"? It's a delete key symbol. Monochrome, code-ish, fits the "operator" theme. U+232B ⌫ ERASE TO THE LEFT. That's a strong "clean/clear" semantic in a digital game: a broom that wipes/clears. Also U+2327 ⌧ X in a rectangle (clear).
- `⌦` U+2326 erase to the right.
- `␡` U+2421 delete.
- `⎚` U+239A clear screen! "CLEAR SCREEN" symbol. That is perfect for a character whose job is clearing lanes: U+239A ⎚. Monochrome, symbol font support (Segoe UI Symbol may have it). It's an obscure glyph though; not obviously "clean".
- `✦` sparkle is a common "clean/shine" sign.

Given the program is "SWEEP.EXE" with a broom kit, a broom-like ASCII mark is the most literal and monochrome. The user is now open to "something that signals cleaning or clean". A sparkle/clean symbol might be less recognizable as a broom but reads as "clean".

I could combine: `✦` with an underscore/brush? Hmm.

They want the center symbol to be simple and readable. Options:
1. ASCII push broom `/---\` + `//////` (literal, our current).
2. `✦` (sparkle/clean) single glyph, monochrome, guaranteed legible at core scale.
3. `⌫` erase key (digital clean).
4. `⌧` clear.

For a cleaning-themed program in a neon terminal game, `✦` is elegant: "clean/spotless" and fits the glyph style of `◎ ▣ ≈`. It's also direction-neutral. But it's not a broom.

The user asked "something that signals cleaning or clean" — sparkle does signal clean. But the program's whole kit is broom pushes; maybe a broom is still better.

Could use `⌁` (electric arrow) no.

Let me test which symbols render monochrome in the font stack and how they look:
- ✦ (U+2726), ✧ (U+2727), ⌫ (U+232B), ⌦, ⎚, ⌧, ✨ (U+2728), ❄ (U+2744), ♲ (U+2672), ⚘, ⸙, ☫.

Test each for color pixels and whether glyph exists (lit pixels). Then pick.

Actually, a nice combo: `✦` inside? The core mark is a single symbol, so `✦` alone.

Alternatively a custom vector broom drawn from lines (not text) — best of both: literal broom, monochrome, scales cleanly. The program's glyph could be a special "drawn" mark. But identity is glyph-based; adding a custom draw path per program is possible (main.ts portrait already draws special accent ticks). For the core mark, we'd branch in render: if program === SWEEP, draw a vector broom rather than drawSymbol. But then the roster's DOM glyph would still show text. Could use `🧹` in text for the roster? Hmm.

Given the user's direction, let's test the symbol candidates and choose one that is monochrome and legible at core size. Then screenshot the card + arena.

Run a canvas test for candidates, checking lit pixels and colored pixels.","open":false,"collapse":"preview"}
{"kind":"tool","id":"ipr_kwiqTx4","toolName":"preview_evaluate","input":{"expression":"(() => { const cands = ['\u2726','\u2727','\u2728','\u232B','\u2326','\u239A','\u2327','\u2744','\u2672','\u2698','\u2E19','\u2318','\u25C7','\u2B21']; const out = []; for (const t of cands) { const c = document.createElement('canvas'); c.width = 64; c.height = 64; const x = c.getContext('2d'); x.font = '700 40px ui-monospace, "Segoe UI Symbol", "Noto Sans Symbols 2", "Apple Symbols", Wingdings, Webdings, sans-serif'; x.textAlign = 'center'; x.textBaseline = 'middle'; x.fillStyle = '#b8ff3a'; x.fillText(t, 32, 32); const d = x.getImageData(0, 0, 64, 64).data; let lit = 0, colored = 0; for (let i = 0; i < d.length; i += 4) { if (d[i+3] > 30) { lit++; if (Math.abs(d[i]-d[i+1]) > 40 || Math.abs(d[i+1]-d[i+2]) > 40) colored++; } } out.push({ t, code: t.codePointAt(0).toString(16), lit, colored }); } return out; })()"}}

{"kind":"tool","id":"ipsYYWO5jxs","toolName":"preview_evaluate","input":{"expression":"(() => { const cands = ['\u2726','\u2727','\u2728','\u232B','\u239A','\u2327','\u2744','\u2672','\u2E19','\u2698','\u{1F9F9}']; const out = []; for (const t of cands) { const c = document.createElement('canvas'); c.width = 64; c.height = 64; const x = c.getContext('2d'); x.font = '700 40px ui-monospace, "Segoe UI Symbol", "Noto Sans Symbols 2", "Apple Symbols", "Segoe UI Emoji", Wingdings, Webdings, sans-serif'; x.textAlign = 'center'; x.textBaseline = 'middle'; x.fillStyle = '#b8ff3a'; x.fillText(t, 32, 32); const d = x.getImageData(0, 0, 64, 64).data; let lit = 0, offTint = 0; for (let i = 0; i < d.length; i += 4) { if (d[i+3] <= 30) continue; lit++; const dr = Math.abs(d[i]-184), dg = Math.abs(d[i+1]-255), db = Math.abs(d[i+2]-58); if (dr+dg+db > 90) offTint++; } out.push({ t, code: t.codePointAt(0).toString(16), lit, offTint }); } return out; })()"}}
{"kind":"reasoning","id":"p66-10fcfbb1","text":"So all the monochrome candidates render in the fill color (good), and the emoji does not.

Now, which symbol best signals cleaning/clean?
- ✦ / ✧ sparkle: "spotless/clean/shine". Common in games for polish/clean.
- ⌫ erase-to-left: digital "wipe", very fitting for SWEEP.EXE clearing lanes; monochrome; reads as a keycap symbol; might be mistaken for a UI hint at the avatar core.
- ⎚ clear screen: obscure.
- ⌧ clear (X in a box): reads as close/delete.
- ♲ recycling: clean/recycle, but more "recycle" than clean.
- ⸙ palm branch: broom-ish (a besom is a bundle of twigs!) — a besom broom is literally a bundle of twigs/branch. ⸙ may render small.
- ⚘ flower: not clean.
- ❄ snowflake: fresh/frost, not cleaning.

Given the kit is a broom and the character is a sweeper, I think `✦` sparkle signals "cleaned" nicely and is a clean, legible single glyph at the core, consistent with `◎ ▣ ≈` in weight and abstraction. But it loses the broom identity.

Alternatively combine a sparkle with the ASCII broom? Too complex.

The user said "expand the symbol search more broadly to look for something that signals cleaning or clean". That implies they want a recognizable clean symbol, not necessarily a broom. `✦` is the classic sparkle/clean. I'd go with `✦` and keep the broom artwork for the kit visuals (swing, projectile, power, skill), so the program still reads as a broom-user while the core says "clean".

Hmm, `✦` is also used for "new"/"favorite"/"sparkle" in UI, and the health hull is lime; a four-point star at the core will read clearly. `✧` (hollow) could pair with the outline style: the hull is outline, so a hollow sparkle fits. But `✧` at 11px radius is thinner and may be less legible. `✦` filled is bolder.

Let me test both in the actual arena: set the Sweep glyph to `✦` and screenshot; then `✧`. But we also have the option of a custom-drawn broom. Given time, choose `✦` with a possible suffix? No.

Wait, there's another thought: a *broom-like* monochrome glyph could be composed from `⋀` over `⋁`? No.

Maybe `⸙` (palm branch) actually looks like a besom broom? It's a small branch with leaves, not a broom.

I'll go with `✦` — it's a clean/spotless mark, monochrome, direction-neutral, and visually distinct from the other programs' marks. I'll note that the only literal broom Unicode is the color emoji, which would break the palette and the no-bitmap rule, so the core mark is a "clean" sparkle while the kit art is the broom.

Hold on: the user's latest instruction is "expand the symbol search more broadly to look for something that signals cleaning or clean" — they may expect me to pick and show it. `✦` is a good choice. Let me also consider `✧` vs `✦`: `✦` filled black four-pointed star = U+2726. In many fonts it's small; at core radius 11.2 with base ~22, single glyph font = 22px, mark ~10px tall. Bold, fine.

Let's implement `glyph: '✦'`, remove glyphRadius (single glyph uses default core radius), keep coreScale ~1.0? For an octagon inradius 20.3, single glyph at font 22 is ~13px wide, fine. Set coreScale 1.05 to make it a bit bigger.

Also remove the multi-line row changes? Keep them; harmless and useful for future ASCII marks. Keep glyphRadius support too, but Sweep no longer uses it. That's fine (small API addition).

Then screenshot the arena and card.

Also the earlier "IN TESTING" label, version, docs, tests, push remain.

Let me make the change.","open":false,"collapse":"preview"}

  if (t % 120 < 60) inputs[0].held |= ACTION.CANDLE;
  world.step(DT, inputs);
  world.clearEvents();
  if (p.broT > 0) sawBro++;
  if (p.fanT > 0) sawFan++;

  }
}

});

- Every gameplay number lives in `src/game/config.ts` and is exported. No magic numbers in `world.ts`.
- A feel change must state the old value, new value, and why in `HISTORY.md`.

- Visual identity: basic shapes only. No bitmaps besides the PWA icon. No sprite sheets. Animation comes
  from rotation, scale, dash afterimages, trail length, color shifts, particles, and shader-free additive
  layering.
- New colors must come from `identity.ts` so player distinctness stays controlled.

Shipped and live at v0.1.37.

**The change you asked for:** a split or merge now dips the local simulation to 0.35x and holds it there for a full second, then eases back to normal over 0.3 s. The camera itself keeps panning at real speed, so the world is near-frozen while your avatar relocates on screen and snaps back to full speed once the frame settles. If the layout changes twice in a row (3 panes → 2 → 1, which happens a lot when bots cluster), each change restarts the dip rather than stacking or cancelling.

It only applies to local modes (training, VS BOTS, gauntlet, campaign). Networked matches never slow, since a guest cannot unilaterally slow a host-authoritative sim, and the stress bench is untouched.

**Verified:**
- `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` clean; `npm run bench` gauntlet 0.251 ms avg / 0.883 ms p99, eight-bot swarm 0.119 / 0.355, all inside the 4 ms budget.
- Local trace of the transition timer: 1.0 s above the slow threshold at 0.35x, 0.3 s easing, back to 1.0.
- GitHub Pages deploy run `41077304879` succeeded, and `spuds0588.github.io/DEFLECT` serves the new bundle (`index-DXS3gW38.js`, `deflect-0.1.37`).
- On production, force-triggering a split (3 panes → 2) started the dip and held a full 1.0 s before easing, measured from the live build.

This screenshot is the shipped 4-pane build on the big arena, with the colored pane frames, one dock per local in the corners and the shared map at top-centre:

![4-pane split on production](screenshots/prod-v037-split2.png)

**What to try on production:** `?autoplay=4&split=4` gives four local panes with bots driving them, so you can see splits and merges happen continuously — that is the only way to see the slow-mo right now, because same-screen input slots don't exist yet. For normal play, a gauntlet on `TRANSIT` or `MAINFRAME` exercises the group framing and the wave look-ahead. The split threshold is `CAMERA.sharedZoomMin` (0.68), `groupPad` (60) and `shareSlack` (70); the dip is `layoutSlowHold` / `layoutSlowTime` / `layoutSlowScale`.

One caveat worth stating plainly: the slow-mo and the merge/split camera are camera plumbing, not playable couch co-op. There is still no second local input slot, so four locals only exist behind the QA hook.

If the dip feels like too much when the layout flaps, the next tuning pass is the hold length plus a minimum gap between dips rather than the scale itself.

- **Pink** (`#ff6ec7`, hot pink held clear of the virus magenta).

## The new geometry

- The reflected shaft leaves at **`PLAYER.laserReflectAngle` = 0.65 rad, about 37.2°** off the incoming line, inside the 30–45° band you asked for.

## What changed in the hit rules

- The caster **no longer takes damage** from the catch. The guard still cuts the charged heavy short into its full 5 s cooldown; the punishment is losing the beam, not eating a hit.

- A body sitting directly behind the guard on the original line is no longer hit, because the deflected line has moved off that axis. In practice, standing behind your guard is now cover for the person behind you, while someone off to the side can still eat it.
- It uses the same beam helpers as the live beam (`beamLineHits`, `damageBeamLine`), so cover cuts the glance exactly where it cuts the drawn shaft.

## 3. Architecture","newString":"The kit is local-only like every other program. It does not add fields to `Snapshot`, and online matches
still run Probe until the protocol carries programs.

### D26 — GHOST.EXE: cloak, chomping mouth, jump-scare (built 2026-10-30)

`GHOST.EXE` is the roster's **stealth** program (id 8, `bugKind` 11). Identity:
`PROGRAM_COLORS.ghost` (`#b9c4d0`, cool steel grey), three outward arcs for the health hull, and a closed
eye at the core. The eye is drawn by `drawGhostEye` as a vector lid with five lashes, never the `◡`
codepoint, so it cannot resolve to a colour emoji or depend on the symbol font; `◡` is only the text
metadata glyph. Its orientation is the bottom-half arc with the lashes hanging below. The hull arcs start
at `0.69r`, curve out to `1.34r`, and leave 120° gaps, so each arc is one health segment and the bright
path never touches the core mark.

- **Ranged**: one wide chomping mouth (type `12`) thrown at `GHOST.shotSpeed` (540, about 40% slower than a
  bolt), 2 damage, `shotRadius` 16, 0.9 s life. It stops on the first body and on cover (it is a committed
  shape in the same geometry-death group as the spear, broom, hourglass and bombs), and it draws the same
  jaw with sharp triangle teeth the whole program uses. A hit dazes the victim: `shotDaze` 0.7 s at
  `shotDazeSlow` 0.55 movement. The daze is a heavy-footed slow, not a root, so the victim can still turn
  and answer late.
- **Skill**: `cloakT` for `cloakTime` 3.5 s. `phased()` gates `damagePlayer`, so shots, blasts, contact
  damage and the void's ordinary damage path all skip the body; AI target picks and sentry/worm/virus
  acquisition skip a cloaked player, while the local renderer keeps a faint dashed readout so the owner can
  navigate. Attacking does not break the cloak. Cloak and the legacy skill-3 ghost timer share the same
  hit gate; do not add a second invisibility flag.
- **Power**: hold the heavy for `scareChargeTime` 0.45 s to re-cloak and arm the jump-scare for
  `scareWindow` 3.2 s. While armed, **any** action press (`BOLT`, `SWING`, `CANDLE` or `DASH`) fires it,
  after which the press is consumed so the same button cannot also act; if the window expires it fires
  nothing. The burst is a cover-respecting `explodeBlast` at `scareRadius` 210, 2 damage and
  `scareKnockback` 1200, drops the cloak, and stamps `SCARE_FACE` at the burst point for `faceTime`
  0.85 s. The charge costs `scareCost` and starts `scareCooldown` when it arms. A release inside
  `heavyTapMax` is the cloak skill instead.
- **Bots**: tap the cloak when a shot is in the air or after a hit, hold the heavy when closing to scare
  range, then chase and press melee once armed. Bots cannot see a cloaked target and re-pick.
- **Renderer**: the mouth has no motion tail and chomps with a per-projectile jaw phase; the cloak is a
  dark disc, dashed rim and faint eye with a heading tick; the armed state adds a pulsing ring and a very
  faint burst radius for the owner; the scare face is ASCII art with O eyes and V teeth over a grey bust.
  The dock uses the closed eye for the skill and an open maw for the heavy.

All numbers live in `tuning/programs.json` under `GHOST`. The kit is local-only like every other program;

+import type { InputFrame } from '../src/game/types';
+
+const bt: InputFrame = { mx: 0, my: 0, held: 0, pressed: 0 };
+const no: InputFrame = { mx: 0, my: 0, held: 0, pressed: 0 };
+const inputs = [bt, no, no, no, no, no, no, no];
+const w = new World(
+  'gauntlet',
+  ['TEST', '', '', ''],
+  0,
+  ARENAS[0],
+  false,
+  0,
+  1,
+  [1],
+  true,
+  FIRST_CAMPAIGN_LEVEL.dataCrates,
+);
+w.friendlyFire = true;
+
+const parents = () => w.sentries.filter((s) => s.active && s.kind >= 4 && s.kind <= 6);
+const children = () => w.sentries.filter((s) => s.active && s.kind >= 7);
+const report = (label: string) => {
+  const kinds = parents().map((s) => `${s.kind}:${s.shapeState}/${s.hp}`);
+  console.log(label, 'phase', w.campaignPhase, 'parents', kinds.join(' '), 'children', children().length, 'hp', w.players[0].hp, 'kills', w.gauntletKills);
+};
+
+report('t=0');
+for (let i = 0; i < 70; i++) w.step(1 / 60, inputs);
+report('t=1.2 wake?');
+for (let i = 0; i < 400; i++) w.step(1 / 60, inputs);
+report('t=7.8');
+
+let maxChildren = 0;
+let echoSeen = 0;
+let shardSeen = 0;
+let damagedAt = -1;
+for (let i = 0; i < 60 * 18; i++) {
+  w.step(1 / 60, inputs);
+  const kids = children();
+  maxChildren = Math.max(maxChildren, kids.length);
+  if (kids.some((s) => s.kind === 7)) shardSeen++;
+  if (kids.some((s) => s.kind === 8)) echoSeen++;
+  if (damagedAt < 0 && w.players[0].hp < w.players[0].maxHp) damagedAt = i;
+  if (i % 120 === 119) report(`t=${(i / 60).toFixed(0)}`);
+}
+console.log('max children', maxChildren, 'shard frames', shardSeen, 'echo frames', echoSeen, 'damagedAt', damagedAt);
+
+const countAtWake = parents().length;
+// Kill the parents through the shared damage path.
+for (const s of parents()) (w as any).damageSentry(s, 9999, 0, 0, 0);
+for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) w.step(1 / 60, inputs);
+console.log('after kill: parents', countAtWake, '->', parents().length, 'phase', w.campaignPhase, 'children', children().length, 'kills', w.gauntletKills, 'drill bots active', w.players.filter((p) => p.active).length);
+console.log('banner', w.campaignBannerKind, 'drill time', CAMPAIGN.drillTime, 'wakeTime', CALIBRATION.wakeTime);

Built and shipped **DISK PLATTER** as arena 09.

It is a 690-radius round platter with nine irregular holes that rotate with the disc at `0.075 rad/s`. The read arm pivots just outside the rim and sweeps across the face on an 11.5 s cycle, shoving players, bots, worms, viruses and sentries without dealing direct damage. A body pushed over a hole or past the rim gets the existing 0.6 s fall grace, so a quick stick input can still save it. Dashing clears a hole, but landing inside one starts the fall.

The plate renders as a true circular floor: rotating servo tracks, sector seams, platter arcs, spindle hub, cut holes with lit lips, rotating rim ticks and the full read arm. The minimap and arena picker use the same hole and arm geometry, so all three views agree.

![DISK PLATTER](screenshots/disk-platter-3.png)

**One gameplay fix from testing:** an idle gauntlet start was dying to a drifting hole at about 8 seconds. Hole 3 was pulled inward to radius 500, keeping every hole inside the 560 spawn ring. An idle run now survives the opening instead of being dropped before the first threat arrives.

**Verification:** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run build` passes, headless checks confirmed the spin, hole fall, arm shove and rim fall, a 60 s HARD bot run recorded 2 deaths and 72 fall ticks, and the production Pages deploy completed successfully. The live production build was checked in DISK PLATTER after the deploy.

**Network note:** hosted rooms keep the round plate and static holes but park the spin and arm, because `Snapshot` carries no disc phase. Local training, gauntlet and campaign runs get the moving floor.

Changes are in [arenas.ts](src/game/arenas.ts), [world.ts](src/game/world.ts), [render.ts](src/game/render.ts), [bot.ts](src/game/bot.ts) and [collision.ts](src/game/collision.ts); docs are updated in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), [README.md](README.md), [TODO.md](TODO.md) and [HISTORY.md](HISTORY.md). Commits `e1990c5` and `26ea977` are pushed to `main`.

The natural next pass is a couch-distance playtest of the arm shove and hole spacing.

pages.yml
---
name: Deploy DEFLECT alpha to Pages

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm

      - name: Install
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      - name: Configure Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: dist

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
---
**Multiplayer menu:** `MULTIPLAYER` offers `ONLINE` (host a room or join by code) and `LOCAL` (same-screen
play, not built yet). Local lists its two modes, `ARENA` and `GAUNTLET`, as placeholders until the setup
screen exists. Public room discovery is planned: it will search for game codes with a shared prefix,
while private rooms keep an unprefixed code.

## Play

The latest main-branch build is deployed to GitHub Pages:

<https://spuds0588.github.io/DEFLECT/>

Run it locally:

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:5173>. Create a room and share the invite link / 4-character code; guests can
join from another tab, browser, or machine that can reach the app.

---
Gameplay tuning lives in [src/game/tuning](src/game/tuning), split into player, program, threat, campaign
and world JSON. `src/game/config.ts` is the typed facade every system imports from, so editing a number is
a JSON change rather than a code change. A running dev server hot-reloads it; see the folder's README for
units, the file map and the values that stay derived in code.

Pushing to `main` builds `dist/` and deploys it to GitHub Pages through
`.github/workflows/pages.yml`. The repository's Pages source must be set to **GitHub Actions**, not the
raw branch.

Architecture, invariants, network protocol, and measured performance live in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).
The forward plan and open design questions are in [TODO.md](TODO.md); session-by-session decisions and
verification are in [HISTORY.md](HISTORY.md). The original specification is
[PRD-Deflect_game.md](PRD-Deflect_game.md).
